text: A message pops up. You feel the pull to reply, but typing feels like too much effort. You just need a quick, low-commitment way to acknowledge it.
Suddenly, three quick reply buttons appear: "Haha!" "Okay!" You tap one instinctively. Instant relief, message sent. It feels so efficient, so perfectly helpful.
You notice a pattern: constantly tapping these buttons. You try to type something unique, but your finger hovers. Why is this simple convenience so hard to resist?
It's a clever system. These buttons drastically reduce interaction friction. Options appear intermittently, hooking your brain into a subtle, unpredictable reward loop.
The cost? You're giving away attention and data with minimal effort. The system learns your patterns, keeping you engaged in a cycle of trivial replies. Your genuine voice gets lost.
Next time those buttons appear, you see past the convenience. You understand the game of friction reduction and intermittent rewards. Now you play on your own terms.
